2. This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail who is apprehending his arrest in relation to FIR/Crime No.256/2024, dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station-Tukoganj,

sentences.text: In view to the said agreement, the society has received Rs.7.00 crores towards guarantee/security for carrying out the construction work.
Complainant has completed the work to the tune of Rs.5.00 crores and a work satisfactory certificate has also been issued by the applicant society.
However, when the complainant party proposed to deposit the post dated cheques, the applicant society has prayed for postponement of depositing the cheques.
Thereafter when the cheques were deposited the same got returned back with remarks of "Stop Payment".
On being enquired it has been informed the construction work was not completed satisfactorily within the stipulated period hence it is a breach of contract therefore the contract was terminated.

therefore, it is a crime of heinous nature and hence, no case is made out for grant of anticipatory bail.

Applicant being director of the society is fully responsible for the illicit act of the society so also she is a resident of State of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12431 4 MCRC-12301-2025 Maharashtra, therefore, if the benefit of anticipatory bail is granted, that may cause hindrance in investigation, hence, Senior counsel prayed for rejection of the bail application.

5. Government Adovcate for the respondent/State has also vehemently opposed the prayer and submitted looking the to nature of the allegation and seriousness of the crime, at this stage no case is made for grant of anticipatory bail.

7. On this aspect the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jai Prakash Singh vs. State of Bihar and others [2012 (4) SCC 379] while canceling the anticipatory bail of the applicant therein so granted concerned High Court, has clearly observed that:-
"13.....The anticipatory bail being an extraordinary privilege should be granted only in exceptional cases.

entities.text: Jai Prakash Singh vs. State of Bihar and others [2012 (4) SCC 379]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The judicial discretion conferred upon the court has to be properly exercised after proper application of mind to decide whether it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Further in para 21 it has been held that:
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12431 5 MCRC-12301-2025 21......The court may not exercise its discretion in derogation of established principles of law, rather it has to be in strict adherence to them.
Discretion has to be guided by law; duly governed by rule and cannot be arbitrary, fanciful or vague.
The court must not yield to spasmodic sentiment to unregulated benevolence.

The order dehors the grounds provided in Section 438 Cr.P.C. itself suffers from non- application of mind and therefore,
cannot be sustained in the eyes of law."
8. In view of the aforesaid, this Court is of the view that at this stage no case is made out for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
7. Accordingly MCRC is dismissed on merits.
